title: Secure wiring and finish the design
target: Document permanent connections and evaluate added mass or friction.
criteria: Check circuit continuity and mechanical security.
Relate a design revision to an energy transfer or force.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A wire joint separates when the battery shifts. What revision addresses both mechanical and electrical reliability?
options: Secure the battery and repair the insulated joint using the supervised procedure.
Bypass the motor with a wire.
Pull the wire tighter across a gear.
Leave exposed wire touching the chassis hardware.
cpa.guide: Mechanical restraint and a secure insulated connection protect the intended circuit.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A motor stops whenever its supply wire is moved. Which testable explanation best fits?
options: Current is permanently consumed by the wire.
Moving a wire always increases battery energy.
An intermittent connection may be opening the circuit.
The motor has become a switch by definition.
cpa.guide: Motion-sensitive loss of operation suggests an intermittent path; inspect safely rather than assuming proof.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A decorative flag clears the wheel when still but bends into it during a run. Which revision should be tested?
options: Shorten or relocate the flag and check clearance during motion.
Tape it to the rotating tire.
Increase rubbing to stabilize it.
Check only its resting position again.
cpa.guide: Dynamic clearance is needed because flexible decoration can move during operation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which finishing plan best preserves a working drivetrain?
options: Hide the switch beneath a permanent panel.
Glue the axle to the chassis.
Cover gears with loose threads.
Keep decorations outside gear and wheel motion and make the switch accessible.
cpa.guide: Finishing must retain mechanical clearance and control access.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A model car’s mass changes from 0.30 kg to 0.36 kg. If net forward force remains 0.90 N, what happens to acceleration?
options: It rises from 3.0 to 3.6 m/s².
It stays 0.90 m/s².
It becomes zero because mass increased.
It falls from 3.0 to 2.5 m/s².
cpa.guide: a = F/m: 0.90/0.30 = 3.0 and 0.90/0.36 = 2.5. The force assumption must be checked in a real car.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: After a decoration is moved away from a wheel, the car travels farther in a coast test. Which explanation is consistent with that evidence?
options: Energy conservation stopped applying.
Less rubbing may transfer less mechanical energy into thermal energy.
The decoration created charge.
Friction vanished everywhere.
cpa.guide: Reducing a contact loss can preserve mechanical energy longer; the trial does not prove every loss disappeared.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
